articles.title: 1989 Aston Martin Lagonda
articles.description: This 1989 Aston Martin Lagonda is a Series 4 example that was initially delivered in Monaco, and it later spent time in Japan and the United Kingdom, where it was refurbished by Nicholas Mee & Company circa 2016. The car was then brought into the United Sates, and it was purchased by the seller six years ago. Finished in Royal Blue over a Magnolia leather interior, the car is powered by a 5.3-liter V8 paired with a three-speed automatic transmission. Additional equipment includes 16″ alloy wheels, fog lamps, a fixed rear sunroof, burl wood veneer interior trim, automatic climate control, digital instrumentation, and an Alpine CD stereo. The car was offered on BaT in July 2023, and maintenance since then has included rebuilding the alternator and addressing an oil leak. This Lagonda is now offered with service records and a Florida title in the seller's name.

articles.title: New App Store Rules Target AI Deepfakes and Nudify Apps
articles.description: Apple today expanded its App Store moderation rules to cover AI-generated nonconsensual intimate imagery. Sexually explicit content was already banned, but now Apple says app developers must proactively prevent and remove AI-generated deepfakes from their platforms. Apple warns that apps with offending content could be removed from the App Store if developers fail to act. The updated 1.2 rule names AI content creation apps and could be targeting apps like Grok, among others. Users have complained about xAI's Grok chatbot being used for nude and sexualized deepfakes, and earlier this year, Apple told xAI it would remove Grok from the App Store if it continued to permit nude deepfakes. xAI put safeguards in place, and Apple approved an updated version of the app. Apple also added guideline 2.5.19 to clarify that developers who add features or functionality not present in the version of an app submitted for review risk removal from the App Store and Apple Developer Program. Apple links the rule to "nudification" apps that create sexually explicit images of real individuals without their consent, suggesting some of the apps have concealed their true purpose during review and added the nudify feature after approval. Apps containing hidden or undocumented features are also prohibited on the App Store, including apps that misrepresent their purpose during review and only reveal harmful capabilities — such as "nudification" — after approval, a tactic commonly known as bait-and-switch. Along with changes focused on AI-generated content, Apple updated section 5 to extend its ban on apps that facilitate human trafficking or child exploitation to alternative app distribution. "We do not hesitate to remove apps, and terminate the developers behind them, when they violate these guidelines," reads Apple's developer news post on the rule changes. Apple's full updated guidelines can be found on its website. articles.title: A teacher saved lives by tackling and fighting the Oregon shooter, police say
articles.description: By Herbert Villarraga and Deborah Bloom BEND, Oregon, Oct 16 (Reuters) - A teacher in the Oregon classroom where a shooter killed three children and an adult threw her cellphone at the shooter, tackled him and fought him in an act that saved lives, police said on Friday. A day into their investigation of the latest U.S. school shooting, authorities released new details of the scene inside a special needs classroom of Silver Rail Elementary School where three school children aged 5, 8 and 11 and a teacher were killed by a 16-year-old former student. Bend Police Chief Mike Krantz did not identify the teacher who fought the assailant, but told a press conference she threw her cell phone at the suspect, tackled him and fought to take his shotgun from him. "She was not injured in that incident, but she almost certainly helped prevent more bloodshed," Krantz said. As the two wrestled, a parent entered the classroom and opened fire on the gunman, killing him. Officials said the parent had followed the shooter into the school, upon witnessing him firing a shotgun from just outside campus. By the time police arrived within three minutes of receiving their first call, the shooter was dead, police said. In the meantime the 16-year-old assailant, who had shot through locked glass doors to enter campus, had killed four people and wounded two others. Krantz, speaking to the heroism shown by the teacher who threw herself onto the suspect and the parent who shot him, said, "I don't think we can underestimate or under-appreciate that courage. When someone is willing to risk their own life for others, we recognize that." He said that the bystander's actions "undoubtedly saved people," and "the teacher who was willing to stand and fight for her children, that's true heroism." Krantz identified the shooter as Griffin J. John II, who was armed with 12-gauge shotgun. He fired about 15 rounds in the classroom and had another 44 rounds on him. The parent who killed the shooter was identified as Kaylub Giamanco, his mother told the New York Times. She identified him as the father of two girls who attend the school, according to video posted by the New York Times of Freeman reading a brief statement. "He is not seeking recognition, but instead wishes to express his gratitude to the first responders, school personnel, and community for the outpouring of love and support," Freeman said. "Kaylub's family, including his two daughters who attend the school, respectfully asks for privacy during this difficult time, and will not be participating in interviews at this time." Residents of Bend, a city of about 100,000 people some 175 miles (280 km) southeast of Portland, gathered near the school to mourn on Friday morning, placing flowers and candles just outside yellow crime scene tape that cordoned off the scene. "Thank God for that father. He saved a lot of lives yesterday, and our prayers should go out for him because he has a lot on his mind today. We wish him well, and thank God for him," Michael Zappa, 71, who lives just blocks from the school, said through tears. Brooke Olsen, the mother of a kindergartener who was safely reunited with her family after the shooting, also expressed gratitude for the man who stopped the shooter. "This is an extremely painful day of grief for everybody in Bend, especially Silver Rail families, and we have to think about what's next for safety measures." Such school shootings have become common in the US, with each one reviving debates over gun laws in a country where a right to "keep and bear Arms" is protected under the Constitution's Second Amendment. Some of the deadliest school attacks in the US include those at Columbine High School in 1999, Sandy Hook Elementary School in 2012, Marjory Stoneman Douglas High School in 2018 and Robb Elementary School in Uvalde, Texas, in 2022. (Reporting by Herbert Villarraga and Deborah Bloom in Bend; Additional reproting by Jonathan Allen in New York and Steve Gorman in Los Angeles; Writing by Daniel Trotta; Editing by Paul Thomasch and Jonathan Spicer) This article originally appeared on Reuters at https://www.yahoo.com/news/us/articles/teacher-tackled-fought-oregon-school-221156030.html
